title.en: TraderBuddy architecture: the stack and the constraints behind it

description.en: What TraderBuddy is made of, and the constraints that shaped it: one WebSocket, thirty symbols, SIP versus IEX, and alerts that need previous state.

children.text: What the system is made of, and the handful of constraints that explain why it is shaped this way rather than some more obvious way.

A self-hosted trading dashboard for about five people: live quotes, server-computed indicators, drawing tools, price alerts delivered to Slack, macro context, and a manual portfolio tracker. It runs on a three-node Talos cluster on Proxmox, behind Cloudflare.
It tracks and alerts. It never trades.

There is no order entry, no broker connection, no paper trading — even though the charting frontend is forked from a project that had all three. The portfolio is a manual ledger you type into. This is a product decision, not a missing feature.

fields.alt: Component architecture: the browser reaches Cloudflare, then a Cilium Gateway API route, which splits traffic between tb-web and tb-api. tb-api talks to Postgres, Valkey, Zitadel and market-data providers. tb-stream holds the single upstream Alpaca WebSocket; tb-alerts and tb-ingest run as scheduled jobs.

children.text: One upstream connection, fanned out through Valkey to every browser.
Real-time is IEX; history is SIP
Live quotes come from IEX, which is a few percent of US volume. Historical bars come from SIP, which is consolidated and authoritative — but the free plan
embargoes the last 15 minutes of SIP
falls inside that window rather than trimming it.
clear of the window for that reason.

The consequence users see: an intraday chart can disagree with an alert until the close, because alerts evaluate SIP bars afterwards. The UI labels which feed a chart is showing instead of pretending they're the same.
(a moving-average cross, a new high, a volume spike, RSI, a percent move) answer a question about a whole session rather than watching 1-minute bars for a touch, so they take their own path:

is pure — daily bars in, a verdict out — and calls the same pandas-ta functions that draw the chart's indicators, so an alert cannot disagree with the line the user is looking at. Daily bars are fetched split-adjusted; level alerts stay on raw prices because a level is a raw price. A condition has no price, so

is nullable, held honest by CHECK constraints, and the chart never draws a line for one. A cross is two consecutive sessions on opposite sides of the line, which is where "previous state" comes from without storing any.

. That distinction requires knowing the previous close, which is why alerts are evaluated once per trading day, server-side, on the session's SIP 1-minute bars — never on ticks, never in the browser. Dragging an alert line past the current price doesn't fire it: the baseline resets and only bars after the edit count.
Money is Decimal, and strings on the wire
is a float to every client. The frontend formats them and does no arithmetic on them.
This is not pedantry. The portfolio ledger's property-based test caught a real bug this way:

Portfolios, alerts and watchlists are scoped to the session user — someone else's id returns

The API is write-only for them — nothing returns a credential, so there is no "show token" — and no admin route touches the table. Webhooks are the one feature that lets a user aim the server at an address of their choosing, in a cluster that also runs Zitadel, Postgres and the Kubernetes API, and

Statements come from SEC EDGAR, which is free and keyless and which the browser never calls. Every request carries a
naming a project contact address, and goes through a Valkey token bucket at 8 requests a second (the SEC allows 10) shared by both API replicas and the nightly job. For a symbol,

changed. A recompute parses the multi-megabyte
30 concepts we map and drops the rest before the next company.

Companies tag the same line differently and change tags over time, so each field takes the first mapped tag that has a value for each period; annual figures are 345–385-day facts with the latest filing winning restatements, and trailing twelve months is the last fiscal year plus this year's year-to-date minus last year's. Indicators and the score are pure functions (

): a piecewise-linear table per indicator, a pillar is the mean of its indicators, and the overall score is the weighted mean of the pillars that could be scored. Unknown is never zero — a missing input is skipped, and fewer than three scored pillars is no score. The report is stored in
block; the nightly scan reads only that block in SQL, never the whole report, which is the memory lesson from 0.4.3. If the SEC is unreachable the stored report is served marked stale.
Each of these is a place the implementation diverged from
on purpose. They are recorded here because an undocumented deviation reads as a bug to the next person.
Profile, metrics and recommendations have identical shape and TTL. Three identical tables would be three places to change.
Hides the candles, adds a baseline series
The drawing manager, crosshair legend and bid/ask lines all hold a reference to the candle series. Removing it would leave them pointing at a disposed object.
